text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Parliament Speaker Berri: The government decisions regarding the audiovisual media law could be better.
-Iranian ambassador: Tel Aviv is trying to impose a new equation in the region.
-SOLIDERE shares to trade on the official Beirut Stock Exchange.
-Israeli soldiers tried to infiltrate into state-controlled areas near the village of Habboush in south Lebanon.
-The situation is relatively calm in the south. The five-nation ceasefire monitoring committee to meet in Naqoura today.
-The government might license one additional television and two radio stations.
-Profit-taking period puts off the rise in SOLIDERE prices.
-The Lebanese army sent commandos to the western part of the Bekaa valley.
-Minister of Oil Barsoumian said the ministry is not currently planning any further increases in the prices of petrol and fuel oil.
